question: Does an accessible official companion report resolve any scientific fish identities from the New Manila Reclamation Project's 2018 Pasig River fish survey?

sourcesReviewed.citation: City Government of Manila. (2018). Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) Report: New Manila Reclamation Project, City of Manila. Official PDF hosted by the DENR Environmental Management Bureau EIA portal.
City Government of Manila. (2018). Public Hearing Documentation Report: New Manila Reclamation Project. Official PDF hosted by the DENR Environmental Management Bureau EIA portal.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed official EMB-hosted indexed PDF text on 2026-11-19. The EIS indexed text exposes the executive summary and table of contents, while the finfish table body pages are not exposed. The companion public-hearing report's indexed text exposes its fish-biota methods, result summary, and photo captions. Direct HTTP HEAD requests to all three official PDF URLs returned 403; no access restriction was bypassed, and no local copy or image was retained.
sourceLocators: 2018 EIS, Executive Summary ES-14: three Pasig River test-fishing operations are summarized as yielding six brackishwater fish species dominated by 'Tilapia'.

2018 EIS, Table of Contents: Table 2-21 is identified as finfish diversity from actual-fishing documentation and key-informant interviews at three Pasig River survey stations (report page 2-160); Table 2-22 is identified as the finfish diversity/CPUE table (report page 2-161). Neither table's rows were retrieved.

2018 Public Hearing Documentation Report, 'Sampling Stations and Methodology: Fish Biota': three stations, 23-24 July 2018; cast net and hook-and-line; in-situ opportunistic identification is described.

2018 Public Hearing Documentation Report, 'Results: Fish Biota': repeats the same three-operation, six-brackishwater-species summary and says 'Tilapia' dominated. This is the same project survey, not an independent dataset.

The hearing report's photo caption names two pest-fish images only as 'knife fish' and 'janitor fish' and says they 'emanate from Laguna Lake'. The caption gives no binomials, vouchers, taxonomic authority, or mapping to the six-species summary; both statements remain unverified source-caption content.
The 2021 alternate official final EIS PDF's indexed search result repeats the executive-summary count but exposed no additional fish table rows.
accessLimits: The indexed EIS body text ends before the report pages containing Tables 2-21 and 2-22; table contents, station coordinates, CPUE, and taxa remain unavailable in this review.
The hearing-report photo captions provide common names only. Photographs were not visually identified, and common names were not converted to scientific names.
The direct 403 responses prevented authorized direct PDF/page-image retrieval in this workflow. No restriction was bypassed.

studyScope.localityContext: Three freshwater-ecology survey stations are described proximal to the BASECO Compound in the City of Manila.
studyScope.methodAsReported: Test fishing with cast net and hook-and-line; opportunistic in-situ identification is described in the companion hearing report.
studyScope.resultAsReported: The project documents report six brackishwater fish species from three test-fishing operations and state that 'Tilapia' dominated. The hearing-report captions separately use the common names 'knife fish' and 'janitor fish' for pest-fish photographs.
studyScope.resultLimit: No species binomials, table rows, per-station taxa, counts, CPUE values, station coordinates, specimen vouchers, or crosswalk between captioned photographs and the six-species summary were recovered.
studyScope.documentRelationship: The EIS and public-hearing documentation concern the same New Manila Reclamation Project and the same July 2018 survey; do not count them as independent confirmations.

decision.disposition: Register the companion official hearing report as an accessible source-level lead, but keep both project documents research-only. The added captions do not resolve scientific identities or recover the underlying fish tables.

limitations: This is a historical, project-specific baseline survey, not a current or complete Pasig River inventory.
The six-species count and 'Tilapia' dominance are executive-summary claims; the supporting finfish rows have not been reviewed.
The words 'knife fish' and 'janitor fish' are ambiguous common-name labels and cannot substantiate scientific identities without the source table or specimen-level crosswalk.
The hearing-report caption's Laguna Lake origin statement is not independently verified and does not provide a demonstrated species identity or movement record.
These documents do not establish current population, catchability, fishing access, legal status, or food safety.
No item-specific reuse license or permission for reproducing tables, photos, maps, or coordinates was verified.
nextActions: Keep the EIS and hearing report catalogued as one project-survey source family; do not count their repeated summary as independent corroboration.
If the official table pages later become available through normal public access, review Tables 2-16, 2-21, and 2-22 together and preserve source spellings and station provenance.
Do not create species or occurrence records from the common-name photo captions or infer scientific identities from the images.
